```java
Collection<CinderDisk> failedRemoveCinderDisks = null;
failedRemoveCinderDisks.addAll(cinderDisks);
```
Reason:
The `failedRemoveCinderDisks` variable is initialized to `null`, and when an exception occurs, the code attempts to call `addAll` on it. Since `failedRemoveCinderDisks` is `null`, this results in a Null Pointer Exception (NPE) because you cannot call methods on a null reference.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
failedRemoveCinderDisks = cinderDisks;
```
Reason:
This change assigns `cinderDisks` directly to `failedRemoveCinderDisks` instead of trying to add elements to it. This ensures that `failedRemoveCinderDisks` is properly initialized with the contents of `cinderDisks`, preventing the NPE when an exception occurs.
